title: Disentangling Sources of Uncertainty in Modeling Saltwater Intrusion Due To Sea Level Rise: The Effects of Model Dimensionality, Physics, and Parameter Choice
content:
Abstract

In coastal aquifers, saltwater intrusion driven by rising sea levels threatens agriculture, ecosystems, and underground infrastructure. Quantifying this process requires numerous modeling decisions that introduce uncertainties; however, most studies only quantify uncertainty due to parameter choices once a modeling approach has been selected. Our goal was to evaluate uncertainties arising from both model and parameter choice when estimating freshwater–saltwater interface movement in response to 1 m of sea-level rise and various changes in groundwater recharge. We compare four modeling approaches applied to one synthetic coastal landscape with homogeneous (but uncertain) hydraulic properties: a 1D + Analytical sharp-interface solution, quasi-2D and quasi-3D sharp-interface models, and a 2D variable-density flow and salt transport model. All numerical models were constructed in MODFLOW 6. Parameter and model-choice uncertainty were calculated using a Moment-Based Global Sensitivity Analysis of interface movement at a centroid cross-section of the coastal watershed. Results indicate that hydraulic conductivity is the dominant source of uncertainty under reduced recharge conditions, followed by aquifer thickness, while the model approach becomes more pronounced under constant or increasing recharge scenarios. These findings highlight the importance of constraining hydraulic conductivity to improve saltwater intrusion predictions. Furthermore, 1D and 2D approaches are limited in capturing out-of-plane and regional flow processes represented in 3D models, and simplified 1D + Analytical models reach full intrusion at lower combined hydraulic conductivity and recharge values than density-dependent models. This study provides guidance for evaluating saltwater intrusion across various modeling frameworks applicable to other coastal watersheds.
